rule: No document other than the canonical one carries the Destructive Fix gate category markers
description: The Destructive Fix Confirmation Gate has exactly one normative enumeration, in security-policy.md. A second normative copy is the defect this fixture exists to catch: two copies drift, one narrows while the other stays broad, and readers of the narrow copy apply a gate that is smaller than the rule. This fixture asserts the NEGATIVE half of that invariant on the documents that cite the gate — safety-rails.md, decision-autonomy.md, overlord.md, drone.md, local-reviewer.md — by requiring each `DESTRUCTIVE-CAT <n>:` marker to occur ZERO times in each of them. expected_counts is shared across a single set_check, so the positive count of one per category in the canonical file and the count of zero per category in the citing files cannot live in the same fixture; this fixture owns the zero half and its companion owns the canonical enumeration. subset mode is what makes the zero half work: it ignores the ten 'missing' members that a marker-free file necessarily reports, while still failing on any captured value outside 1 through 10, so a marker numbered 11 pasted into a citing file is an extra and fails here too. The capture group is a negated-delimiter class anchored on the marker rather than a positive charset, so a copied marker cannot be invisible to the check by virtue of how its number is written. The source pin carries the sentence in safety-rails.md that states the prohibition and its reason in one clause — 'This section never restates the categories: the second copy is exactly what let one copy narrow while the other stayed broad' — so deleting the rule, or keeping the rule while deleting the reason that justifies it, stops the pattern matching. The consumers entries pin the canonical file's own two structural claims: that its list is the single canonical statement of the categories, and that the list's shape is one line per category, numbered 1 through 10, with no duplicates. Both are claim-carrying: the first is the uniqueness assertion the citing documents rely on, the second is the shape that makes the marker-set assertion in the companion fixture meaningful. overlord.md and local-reviewer.md reach the gate through safety-rails.md's retained pointer section rather than citing security-policy.md directly; that is resolving indirection, not a dangling reference. RESIDUALS, stated plainly: an UNMARKED verbatim re-copy of the ten rows — the same category text without the `DESTRUCTIVE-CAT <n>:` markers — is invisible here, because no fixture in this directory can assert body-prose ABSENCE (`absent` is scoped to YAML frontmatter), and the counted markers are the only handle this mechanism has. set_check `files` is a literal list with no glob expansion, so a marked copy planted in a document this fixture does not name is likewise invisible; the protection is real for the five named files and blind to new ones. Every pin here claims word-sequence presence, never meaning, so prose that keeps the pinned sentences intact while contradicting them elsewhere passes.

source.pattern: This section never restates the categories: the second copy is exactly what let one copy narrow while the other stayed broad.

consumers.pattern: This list is the ONE canonical statement of the gate categories
one line per category, numbered 1 through 10, no duplicates
